reference: User-provided WorldBox screenshot used for high top-down projection and low-noise value grouping only; no pixels extracted.

steps.purpose: Flatten initial tall mountain draft into low connected outcrops
steps.prompt:
EDIT image 1 (the four snow mountain clusters atlas). Image 2 is ONLY a visual style reference showing the high top-down view, small-scale craggy snowy outcrops and restrained pixel clusters; do not copy or extract any pixels from it.
Critical change: image 1 is still far too frontal, tall and like alpine mountain icons. REDRAW ALL FOUR OBJECTS as VERY LOW, HIGH TOP-DOWN SNOWY ROCK OUTCROPS. We look almost straight down, so the footprint is broad and the visible south/right cliff face is only about 10 to 20 percent of object height. No triangular pyramid summits, no conical mountains, no repeated snowcap mountain emoji. Think a broken slab or low craggy plateau with 3 to 5 uneven joined ridges, with broad snow-covered top planes and short angular blue-gray side faces. Slightly uneven rounded-angular pixel silhouette. Dark bedrock foot merges into a flat dark-gray map. Snow should occupy 55 percent of each irregular outcrop, with coherent quiet connected offwhite planes, 2 or 3 broad blue-gray crevices between raised ledges, dark rock saddles connecting the forms. Visible depth through adjacent lit top and short shaded edge, not through height.
Preserve: FOUR different arrangements, 2x2 grid, transparent background and margins, same consistent top-left light and muted offwhite / pale-blue-gray / slate / charcoal palette. Original low-resolution pixel art, designed for 48x40 pixels per object. Broad deliberate pixel shapes, few details. Never add little pebbles, scattered flecks, fine veins, V-shaped repeat textures, grain, speckling, dithering, text or labels. Each object has ONE irregular solid silhouette, not a carpet tile. No scenery. Overall closely match the top-down terrain projection visible in reference image 2, while making new original shapes.

steps.purpose: Prepare solid chroma key instead of a baked checker background
steps.prompt: Change ONLY the background of this four-object sprite sheet to a perfectly solid vivid magenta #ff00ff. Remove all checkerboard squares. Preserve the four snow-covered rocky outcrop drawings, their shape, snow caps, colors, shadows, arrangement and proportions exactly. No new shading, no outline, no magenta inside the objects, no magenta tint on edges. The object silhouettes should have hard clean edges against the pure magenta key background. This is technical game sprite background preparation, not an art redesign. Keep all four objects complete, a 2 by 2 grid, with gutters. No text or border.

steps.purpose: Give snow caps geological planes instead of cloud-shaped lobes
steps.prompt:
Refine the FOUR snow-rock outcrop sprites in this atlas while preserving the exact 2x2 cell layout, outer footprint, top-down low viewpoint, size, muted palette, dark rock feet and solid #ff00ff background.
The current white caps look too much like soft five-lobed clouds or flowers. Make them geological: each object should have an asymmetrical elongated main snow ridge broken into two or three broad angular planes, with one uneven narrow blue-gray exposed crease connecting to a shaded side. Some white areas narrow to a short tongue along a ledge; other areas are interrupted by a dark exposed rock notch. Use gently stepped pixel contours with a few squared facets instead of fluffy round lobes. Separate bright upper-left facing snow, muted blue-gray right-facing snow and dark rock consistently. Keep about 45 percent of each object offwhite, 20 percent pale cool-gray, remaining exposed stone. Detail should describe the actual ridge direction, NEVER decorate the surface. FOUR genuinely different outcrop shapes and different ridge bends, same illumination, all viewed from above. No conical triangular mountain icons, no repeating V patterns, no checkerboard, no scattered pebbles, no noise, no speckles, no thin outlines, no added background or labels. True restrained pixel art for small 64x48 game sprites.

normalization: Chroma key, fixed 2x2 slicing, six-colour palette, binary alpha, 64x48 frames. No procedural drawing of peak art.
